name: Amankila
positioning: Aman resort of standalone villa suites on a hillside on Bali's rural east coast, with a private black sand Beach Club
best_for: Travelers who want a quiet, rural stretch of Bali's east coast rather than the busier south
Guests who value a private black sand beach and hillside villa suites over a full spa

facts.text: Amankila is on Bali's less-explored, truly rural east coast.
Amankila is one of the original Aman resorts, and its name means "peaceful hill".
The accommodation is standalone, alang-alang-roofed villa suites staggered on a hillside.
Sandikala is the signature dining venue, on the hillside with views of the Lombok Strait.
The open-air restaurant serves just-caught seafood, suckling pig, satay skewers and sambals.
Traditional Afternoon Tea is served every afternoon at The Bar, with treats handmade by mothers from a nearby village.
Batu Jati Sunset is a cocktail and canape experience on the Batu Jati Rock Platform overlooking the Lombok Strait and the black sand beach.
There is an outdoor gym and a lap pool.
The accommodation listing includes round-trip transfers from Bali International Airport (DPS).
Use of non-motorised watersports equipment at the Beach Club is included.

highlights.text: The Beach Club occupies a stretch of private black volcanic sand.
The three-tier infinity pool was designed with inspiration from the nearby water palace at Ujung and sacred Mount Agung.
The Beach Dinner offers two candlelit tables on the sand, each with its own chef grilling over open flame.
The Megibung Dinner is an East Balinese sharing tradition centred on Nasi Tumpeng, a cone-shaped rice offering symbolising Mount Agung.
Architect Ed Tuttle's walkways zig-zag up the hillside, and the resort uses thatching and paras-stone walls.

considerations.text: There is no spa, but Balinese massage and wellness sessions, including yoga, can be booked.
